tour.title: Choose where code runs
tour.text: Each tab runs on a target: the bundled Laravel sandbox, a project on this Mac, a Docker container, or an SSH host. Pick one here; File ▸ Open Project… adds a project. Switching runs nothing.

tour.title: Write PHP and run it
tour.text: Type code in the editor and press Run. Run Selection runs only the selected lines. Nothing runs until you ask.

tour.title: Read the output
tour.text: Structured shows dumps and results as cards you can expand, Plain is a transcript like the command line, and Raw is exactly what PHP wrote. After a run, the queries it ran, the mail it sent, and its log messages show here too.

tour.title: History, snippets, and the database
tour.text: Every run is kept in History. Save code you reuse as a snippet, for yourself or for the project. The Database pane lists a connection's tables once you load them.

tour.title: Open Anything
tour.text: Switch targets, and open snippets, recent files, and past runs. Type > for every command, or press ⇧⌘P.

tour.title: SQL, Redis, and MongoDB tabs
tour.text: A tab can also hold SQL, Redis commands, or a MongoDB query: File ▸ New SQL Tab, New Redis Tab, or New MongoDB Tab. Redis and MongoDB tabs have a builder (⌥⌘B) that writes the command for you.

tour.title: Everything that's open
tour.text: The status bar counts SSH logins, tunnels, database sessions, runs, and AI clients. Click it to open the Connection Manager, where each has Close.

tour.title: Settings
tour.text: Appearance, the editor, PHP, Docker, AI clients, and shortcuts are in Settings. Help ▸ Show Tour plays this tour again, and Help ▸ What's New shows what changed.

also: This release contains no user-facing changes.
The Profiles window's buttons show their full labels when you have no profiles yet.
Runlet takes about 70 MB less space on disk: stable releases leave out the debugging symbols.
Runlet runs on macOS 15 (Sequoia) and later, not only macOS 26 and later.
0.4.0 is the stable release of betas 1 to 8, with nothing new since beta 8. Settings ▸ General ▸ Updates can switch to the Stable channel, which offers only stable releases.

features.title: In-app updates
features.text: Runlet ▸ Check for Updates… finds a newer version, shows its release notes, and installs it with Install and Relaunch, keeping the old version until the new one starts. Settings ▸ General ▸ Updates has the channel, Stable or Beta, and automatic checks.

tour.title: Check for updates
tour.text: Choose Runlet ▸ Check for Updates…, or Check for Updates in Open Anything. Updates are signed and checked before anything is installed, and one found by an automatic check waits until no code runs.

tour.title: Stable or Beta
tour.text: Settings ▸ General ▸ Updates picks the channel: Stable gets releases, Beta gets pre-releases too. Automatic checks run at launch and once a day; Check Now runs one.

features.title: A guided tour, and this window
features.text: A short tour on the first launch points at the real controls, and after an update this window shows what changed, with Show Me tours. Help ▸ Show Tour and Help ▸ What's New open them any time.

tour.title: Replay the tour
tour.text: Help ▸ Show Tour, or Show Tour in Open Anything, walks through the main window again. Settings ▸ General ▸ Tips turns the first-launch tour and What's New off.

releases.label: 0.4.0 beta 7

features.title: Log viewer
features.text: View ▸ Logs (⌘L) shows a target's logs, parsed: Laravel's and Symfony's log files, WordPress's debug.log, and a container's or server's output once you click Follow. Filter by level, search, or show only what the last run added.

tour.title: Open the Logs window
tour.text: View ▸ Logs, or Logs in Open Anything. Reading files on this Mac runs nothing; a container or a server is followed only when you click Follow, and Stop ends it.

features.title: Dry Run
features.text: Runs a PHP tab in database transactions that Runlet always rolls back, then says how many statements it undid. On MySQL, statements that would commit the transaction are refused before they run.

tour.title: Turn on Dry Run
tour.text: Click Dry Run in a PHP tab's toolbar. While it's on, every run of the tab rolls back its database changes. Turning it on runs nothing.
tour.menu: Run ▸ Dry Run (Roll Back Database Changes)

tour.title: See what was rolled back
tour.text: After the run, the Dry run card lists each connection's statements, and warns about anything that couldn't be rolled back.

features.title: Source excerpts in error cards
features.text: Error cards show the lines around the failing line, and Thrown in shows the file where it happened. Stack frames open to their source, and clicking a line goes there.

tour.title: The code where it failed
tour.text: When a run fails, its error card shows the lines around the failing line. Click a line to go to it; ▸ on a stack frame shows its code.

features.title: Move and duplicate lines
features.text: ⌥↑ and ⌥↓ move the current line, or every selected line, in every tab language. ⇧⌥↑ and ⇧⌥↓ duplicate them. Both are in Edit ▸ Lines.

tour.title: Move lines with ⌥↑ and ⌥↓
tour.text: Put the caret on a line, or select several, and press ⌥↑ or ⌥↓. Add ⇧ to duplicate them instead. Each press is one undo step.

also: The run inspector's Log section has Show in Logs Window, and Logs is in Open Anything.
File locations in log entries are links that open like the stack frames of error cards.

releases.label: 0.4.0 beta 6

features.title: Redis and MongoDB builders
features.text: View ▸ Show Builder (⌥⌘B) opens a form beside the editor: about 150 Redis commands with their options, or a MongoDB query with filters, projection, sort, pipeline stages, and updates. It writes the text into the tab and never runs anything.

tour.title: Open the builder
tour.text: In a Redis or MongoDB tab, click Builder or press ⌥⌘B. Fill in the form; Insert or Replace Line writes the command, and every MongoDB change rewrites the query as one undo step.

features.title: Code navigation
features.text: Go to Definition (F12 or ⌘-click), Find References (⇧F12), code actions (⌥↩), inlay hints, and folding in PHP tabs, from PHPantom. Vendor code and files on Docker or SSH targets open in a read-only peek.

tour.title: Jump to a definition
tour.text: ⌘-click a class, function, or method, or put the caret on it and press F12. ⇧F12 lists its references, and ⌥↩ shows code actions such as Import class.

tour.title: Fold blocks, show hints
tour.text: Fold a function, array, or comment with ⌥⌘← and unfold it with ⌥⌘→ (Edit ▸ Code Folding). View ▸ Show Inlay Hints turns parameter names and types on or off.

tour.title: PHPantom's status
tour.text: PHPantom indexes the tab's project and says here when it's ready. Library ▸ Restart Language Server restarts it.

features.title: Queued runs
features.text: Runlet runs four runs at once. One waiting for a free slot shows as Queued in the Connection Manager and in its tab's status bar, and the status bar's hourglass counts them.

tour.title: Active and queued
tour.text: The number counts what's open; an hourglass with a number appears while runs wait for a slot. Click it to see them, with Close on each.

also: Redis completion: commands with their syntax, subcommands, options, and the keys Runlet has already scanned. Typing never queries Redis.
.redis project snippets and personal Redis snippets, with # @title, # @connection, and # @input.
Project snippets reload when .runlet/snippets changes.
Connections from this Mac pick a local PHP that has the connection's driver.
MongoDB's find applies projection and sort again.

releases.label: 0.4.0 beta 5

features.title: Redis and MongoDB tabs
features.text: File ▸ New Redis Tab and New MongoDB Tab. Commands and JSON queries run on the application's connection or one you saved, with structured replies, a key or collection browser, and a server panel. Dangerous commands always ask first.

tour.title: Open a Redis or MongoDB tab
tour.text: Choose File ▸ New Redis Tab or New MongoDB Tab. A .redis file opens as a Redis tab too.

tour.title: Pick its connection
tour.text: The application's own connection needs no credentials from Runlet; a saved one keeps its password in the Keychain. Read-only connections refuse writes.

features.title: Database tools
features.text: The Database pane's Server section shows the server, its sizes, and its sessions, with Kill and Cancel. A table's menu has Browse Table (pages read on the server, edits reviewed as SQL first), Show Definition, and Show Relations.

tour.title: The Database pane
tour.text: Database shows the tab's connection: Tables, and the Server section. Loading the schema and reading the server are always a click, and Kill and Cancel always ask.

features.title: Connection Manager
features.text: Window ▸ Connections (⇧⌘C) lists everything Runlet has open: SSH logins, tunnels, database sessions, runs, and AI clients, each with Close. The status bar counts them.

tour.title: Click the count
tour.text: The status bar shows how many connections are open; its tooltip has them by kind. Click it to open the Connection Manager.

features.title: Notices, warnings, and errors
features.text: \Runlet\notice(), warning(), and error() put cards in the output without stopping the run, with a link to the line that called them. The snippet API reference is in docs/snippet-api.md.

tour.title: Your own cards
tour.text: Call \Runlet\warning('Slow query', $context) and a warning card appears here, linked to its line, with $context as a value you can expand.

features.title: Import from TablePlus
features.text: Imports SQL, Redis, and MongoDB connections from TablePlus, and can create the SSH profiles they use; copying passwords is up to you. It's behind a feature flag in Settings ▸ Advanced.

tour.title: Turn on the feature flag
tour.text: Press ⌥⌘, to open Settings on Advanced, and turn on Import connections from TablePlus. Import from TablePlus… then appears in Settings ▸ Databases and Edit Connections.

also: Saved connections can open from this Mac, or through an SSH profile's tunnel, and can be offered on every target, the sandbox included.
Stop cancels the running statement on MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, and MongoDB servers.
CSV export of a whole query, CSV import into a table, and every result set of a stored procedure.
Run History and SQL snippets remember their connection.
SQL tabs on WordPress use its own PDO connection, and wp_mail() is recorded.
The mail chip shows the tab's mail mode and switches it.

releases.label: 0.4.0 beta 4

features.title: Explain Statement
features.text: Run ▸ Explain Statement (⌥⌘E) shows the plan of the statement at the caret as a tree, full scans highlighted, without running it. Explain Analyze runs it, and asks first when it could write.

tour.title: Explain the statement at the caret
tour.text: In an SQL tab, put the caret in a statement and press ⌥⌘E. The plan opens in the output, and nothing runs.

also: SQL results, PHP tables, and the result window draw only the rows on screen, so large results scroll smoothly.
A parameters drawer under the SQL editor binds :name and ? values; they're never written into the SQL.
Saved connections can be read-only, enforced by the database, with their own environment and colour.
TLS, Unix sockets, charsets, init statements, SQL Server, and custom PDO DSNs for saved connections.

features.title: Saved database connections
features.text: Save MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL, and SQLite connections for a project, a Docker profile, or an SSH host. SQL tabs, completion, and the schema explorer use them, and their passwords stay in the macOS Keychain.

tour.title: Open an SQL tab
tour.text: Choose File ▸ New SQL Tab. Its statements run on a connection, never through a shell.

tour.title: Pick a connection
tour.text: Choose the application's own connection, or one you saved. New Connection… adds one, with Test Connection; production targets still ask before each run.

releases.label: 0.4.0 beta 2
also: Format Code (⌥⇧⌘F) formats a PHP tab with the bundled Mago formatter; its styles are in Settings ▸ Editor ▸ Formatting.
File ▸ Save as Artisan Command… and Save as Test… turn a snippet into a file in its project, through a save panel.
The DMG has an Applications shortcut: drag Runlet onto it to install.

releases.label: 0.4.0 beta 1

features.title: Schema explorer
features.text: Library ▸ Database (⇧⌘B) lists a connection's tables and views, with their columns, keys, and indexes. Double-click a table to open its first rows as a query in a new SQL tab; it runs only when you press Run.

tour.title: Load the schema
tour.text: The Database pane shows what is loaded; loading is always a click on Load. Then filter the tables and open one.

also: Open in Window on any result table: search, filter rules, sorting, and CSV of the rows shown.
Type dark, light, or auto in Open Anything (⌘P), or use View ▸ Appearance.
A run of 10 seconds or more that finishes in the background posts a notification (Settings ▸ General ▸ Notifications).
